action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

**2024 update:** The page doesn't describe a distinct 2024 feature update. It lists 2024 as the year of battery-electric (EV) changes: the EV variants use an 83 kWh LFP CATL battery, with CLTC range of 602–620 km for rear-wheel drive and 534–552 km for all-wheel drive. The page also says the 2025 facelift's powertrain is "unchanged compared to the 2024 model."

**M5 Ultra (2025 facelift)**

*Dates*
- Announced March 1, 2025, with pre-orders opening the same day.
- Launched March 20, 2025, with deliveries starting April 3.

*Exterior*
- Two new paint colors, Phantom Purple and Zero-Degree White.
- An optional Obsidian visual package adds black-painted wheels, badge, lower grille, and window trim.

*Interior*
- A column-mounted shifter frees 14.4 L of open storage under the center console.
- The front passenger seat gains a four-way adjustable legrest.
- Cupholders are now separate side-by-side units.
- Wireless charging pads are upgraded to 50 W, and the USB-C outlet outputs 100 W.
- A new Red Tea Orange seat upholstery option is available.

*ADS and sensors*
- Every variant includes Huawei's "ADS 3.3 ADAS system as standard."
- Sensor upgrades include one new 192-line LiDAR and five 4D mmWave radars.
- Capabilities include supervised autonomous driving on highways and in urban areas, automatic emergency braking in all directions, automatic emergency steering, and remote-control parking.
- AITO claims "81% smoother braking."

*Sales*
- 15,000 pre-orders were reported on April 30, 2025.
- Deliveries passed 10,000 by June 1, 2025.

**2025 Xpeng G6**

- **Battery:** Xpeng did not state capacity at launch. The MIIT catalog lists 68.5 kWh for the 625 km variant and 80.8 kWh for the 725 km variant. The article gives no predecessor capacity.
- **Charging:** Upgraded from 3C to 5C. It "can charge from 10 percent to 80 percent in 12 minutes," versus "as little as 20 minutes" for the previous G6.
- **Range (CLTC):** 625 km on the two lower variants, 725 km on the top variant.
- **Driving assistance:** The "free Turing AI smart driving System" is standard, with 2 Nvidia Drive Orin chips and 508 TOPS. LiDAR was removed, "shifting to a pure vision solution."
- **Performance:** Single-motor rear-wheel drive, 218 kW peak power, 450 Nm peak torque. 0–100 km/h takes 6.4 s (lower variants) or 6.3 s (top variant). The article gives no predecessor figures.
- **Dimensions and platform:** 4,758 mm long (predecessor 4,753 mm), 1,920 mm wide, 1,650 mm high, 2,890 mm wheelbase, 800-volt platform.
- **Price:** Starts at RMB 176,800, which is RMB 23,100 (11.56%) below the predecessor's RMB 199,900 starting price.
- **Not covered:** Screens, suspension, and design changes beyond dimensions.

**2025 Xpeng G9**

- **Battery:** 79 kWh, 93.1 kWh, and 93.1 kWh across the three variants, per the MIIT catalog. The article gives no predecessor capacity.
- **Charging:** 5C, with 10% to 80% in "as little as 12 minutes," versus "as little as 20 minutes" for the 2024 G9.
- **Range (CLTC):** 625 km and 725 km (single-motor), 680 km (dual-motor).
- **Suspension:** "dual-chamber air suspension as standard." The 2024 G9 had air suspension only on its top variant.
- **Driving assistance:** Same as the G6: free Turing system, 2 Orin chips, 508 TOPS, LiDAR removed.
- **Performance:** Single-motor models have 258 kW and 465 Nm, with 0–100 km/h in 6.6 s or 6.4 s. The dual-motor model has 423 kW, 695 Nm, and 4.2 s. The article gives no predecessor figures.
- **Dimensions and design:** 4,891 mm long, 1,937 mm wide, 1,670 mm high, 2,998 mm wheelbase (unchanged). The article calls it the "facelifted G9" but describes no specific exterior design changes.
- **Price:** Starts at RMB 248,800, which is RMB 15,100 (5.72%) below the 2024 starting price of RMB 263,900.
- **Not covered:** Screens and interior changes.

content.content: 27 rows

**Geely Galaxy L6 EM-i (launched February 12, 2025)**

- **Powertrain:** The refresh uses the NordThor 2.0 (Leishen 2.0) plug-in hybrid system, first introduced with the Starship 7. Unlike the original turbocharged L6, it uses "a naturally aspirated engine rather than a turbocharged unit," which the article says is meant to compete more directly with the BYD Qin L's DM-i 5.0 system.
- **Engine and motor:** A 1.5-litre naturally aspirated four-cylinder makes 82 kW (110 hp), paired with a DHT transmission and an integrated P3 motor rated at 160 kW (215 hp). The system's peak output is also 160 kW (215 hp).
- **Battery and range:** Buyers can choose an 8.5 kWh CALB pack or a 19.1 kWh SVOLT pack. The article gives CLTC electric ranges of 48 km (30 mi) and 115 km (71 mi), respectively, and a combined range of 1,300 km (808 mi).
- **Performance:** The smaller-battery version reaches 0–100 km/h in 7.4 seconds. Both versions have a top speed of 180 km/h.
- **Exterior:** Dimensions are unchanged. The main visible update is a switch to loop-style door handles.
- **Interior:** The central display is a "horizontally-oriented 14.6-inch screen," replacing the earlier vertical 13.2-inch unit. Below it sit "a pair of air vents and two wireless charging pads" plus a panel with a rotary dial and other controls. The steering wheel is a new two-tone, two-spoke design, and the center console has been redesigned.

**Date:** Launched February 14, 2025 (article published February 15, 2025).

**Comparison with the previous Galaxy L7**

The article gives a baseline only for the design and dimensions. It does not state the previous model's powertrain, range, screens, or chip, so those items below are listed as features of the new EM-i without a direct comparison.

- **Design:** Built on the Galaxy L7 platform, with a "through-type LED headlight group" and a closed front panel. An EM-i logo is added to the tail.
- **Dimensions:** 4710/1905/1685 mm, with a 2785 mm wheelbase that is "10 cm longer than the previous model." Curb weight is 1810–1890 kg depending on trim.
- **Hybrid system:** "Geely's new generation NordThor hybrid system."
  - **Version 1:** 1.5L naturally aspirated engine, 82 kW (110 hp)/136 Nm; 160 kW (215 hp)/262 Nm motor; E-DHT transmission; 18.4 kWh LFP battery.
  - **Version 2:** 1.5T engine, 120 kW (161 hp)/255 Nm; 107 kW (143 hp)/338 Nm motor; 3DHT Pro transmission; 18.7 kWh LFP battery.
- **EV range:** 115 km CLTC electric range for both versions.
- **Fuel consumption and total range:** WLTC 1.05–1.3 L/100 km; comprehensive range of 1,240 km.
- **Charging:** Official claim of 20 minutes for 30% to 80% in fast charging mode; slow charging takes 2.7–3 hours.
- **OS:** Flyme Auto intelligent cockpit system.
- **Screens (standard across the series):** 10.25-inch LCD instrument panel, 13.2-inch central screen, and 16.2-inch co-pilot entertainment screen, with dual-screen linkage, CarLink, and HiCar phone interconnection.
- **Chip:** Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155, not Geely's own Dragon Eagle-1.
- **Interior:** Four-spoke steering wheel; two theme colors, brown and gray.
- **Price:** Limited-time 115,800–148,800 yuan (16,000–20,500 USD).
- **ADAS:** Not mentioned in the article.

**Launch date:** October 25, 2024

**Powertrain**
- **Hybrid system:** The SUV moves to BYD's DM 5.0, which the article says is "upgrading the SUV to its latest DM 5.0 hybrid system." It is said to lower fuel consumption, but no figure is given, and the predecessor's system isn't named.
- **Engine:** 1.5 L, 115 kW max power, 225 Nm peak torque (standard). No prior engine figures are given for comparison.
- **Motor:** Front-mounted single motor, 200 kW peak power, 315 Nm peak torque. No prior motor figures are given.
- **Acceleration:** 0 to 100 km/h in 7.5 seconds.

**Battery and range**
- **EV range:** 115 km (CLTC) on each variant.
- **Combined range:** 1,150 km on a full tank and full charge.
- Battery capacity and fuel consumption figures are not stated.

**Pricing (vs. Tang DM-i Glory Edition, launched February 28)**
- Entry variant: RMB 179,800 ($25,250), unchanged.
- Second variant: RMB 187,800 (down RMB 2,000 from RMB 189,800).
- Third variant: RMB 197,800 (down RMB 2,000 from RMB 199,800).
- Top variant: RMB 207,800 (down RMB 12,000 from RMB 219,800).

**Body**
- Seven seats; 4,870 × 1,950 × 1,725 mm; 2,820 mm wheelbase. The article gives no predecessor dimensions to compare against.

**Not covered:** The article says nothing about ADAS, design, or screen changes, so I can't confirm any differences in those areas.

The article says all BYD-brand models got the update with prices unchanged, so the smart driving features were added at no extra cost.

**God's Eye tiers**

BYD calls its smart driving system "God's Eye," with three tiers:

- **God's Eye A (DiPilot 600):** Uses three LiDARs and is mainly used by Yangwang.
- **God's Eye B (DiPilot 300):** Uses one or two LiDARs and is mainly used by Denza and some premium BYD models.
- **God's Eye C (DiPilot 100):** "does not have any LiDAR and instead uses a camera vision solution," and is aimed at BYD's affordable models.

The article doesn't say which God's Eye tier each model in your list uses. It also doesn't mention radars, chips, NOA, or parking features for any of them.

**Other relevant details**

- BYD's DM hybrid and e pure-electric platforms were upgraded to Xuanji Architecture to support God's Eye C.
- BYD says 5,000+ engineers spent seven years on R&D for the system.
- BYD says over 4.4 million vehicles have L2 or more capable systems.

- Dolphin length change (+130mm)

content.content:
**Date:** September 23, 2024 (launch event; the article is dated Sept 23, 2024, 6:25 PM GMT+8)

**Note:** The article calls the predecessor the "Glory Edition," not "Honor Edition."

**Comparison with the Song Pro DM-i Glory Edition (from the article):**

- **Pricing:** The new model starts at RMB 112,800 ($15,980), which is RMB 3,000 (2.7%) above the Glory Edition's RMB 109,800 starting price.
- **Variants:** Four variants, one fewer than the Glory Edition's five.
- **Dimensions:** 4,735 mm long, 1,860 mm wide, 1,710 mm high, 2,712 mm wheelbase. It is slightly shorter than the predecessor's 4,738 mm length.
- **DM 5.0:** The article says the new model is based on the DM 5.0 system but doesn't say whether the Glory Edition used it.
- **Powertrain:** 1.5 L engine (74 kW) and an electric motor (120 kW, 210 Nm peak torque). 0–100 km/h in 8.3 or 8.5 seconds. The article doesn't give predecessor figures for comparison.
- **EV range:** Blade battery options of 12.9 kWh and 18.3 kWh, with CLTC pure electric ranges of 75 km and 115 km. No predecessor range is given.
- **Combined range:** Not stated for the Song Pro DM-i.
- **Fuel consumption:** 3.79 L per 100 km under NEDC at low power, the same as the Sealion 05 DM-i.

**Not covered in the article:** combined range for the Song Pro, design changes beyond dimensions, tail lights, screen size, wireless charging, and ADAS/DiPilot.

**God's Eye C / DiPilot 100:** The article doesn't describe highway NOA, navigate-on-autopilot, parking, camera or radar counts, chip, or compute. The only relevant sentence is about the system's hardware approach:

- "DiPilot 100, which does not have any LiDAR and instead uses a camera vision solution" (the article also says it's for BYD's affordable models)

**Seagull, Dolphin, Qin Plus, Song L, Yuan Up:** The article lists these only with price ranges.

- Seagull: "Seagull Smart Driving Edition: RMB 69,800 to RMB 85,800."
- Seagull (summary): "including the Seagull, which is priced as low as RMB 69,800."
- Dolphin: "Dolphin Smart Driving Edition: RMB 99,800 to RMB 125,800."
- Qin Plus (DM-i): "Second-generation Qin Plus DM-i Smart Driving Edition: RMB 79,800 to RMB 103,800."
- Qin Plus (EV): "Second-generation Qin Plus EV Smart Driving Edition: RMB 109,800 to RMB 129,800."
- Song L (DM-i): "Song L DM-i Smart Driving Edition: RMB 135,800 to RMB 175,800."
- Song L (EV): "Song L EV Smart Driving Edition: RMB 189,800 to RMB 249,800."
- Yuan Up: "Yuan Up Smart Driving Edition: RMB 99,800 to RMB 119,800."

The article uses "Yuan Up," not "Yuan Plus."

**发布日期：** 2024年7月22日（IT之家报道，比亚迪海洋网销售事业部总经理张卓当日公布官图，车型7月25日上市）

**相对现款的变化（依据原文）：**

- **技术定位：** 采用第五代DM混动技术，官方称其为"第五代 DM 技术首款 SUV"。原文没有"DM 5.0"的说法。
- **外观：** 与现款基本一致，车尾标识由"BUILD YOUR DREAMS"缩为"BYD"。
- **发动机：** 1.5升发动机最大功率74千瓦，比现款降低7千瓦。
- **驱动电机：** 最大功率160千瓦，比现款提升15千瓦。
- **纯电续航（WLTC）：** 提升至91km（18.3kWh版）与128km（26.6kWh版）。
- **油耗：** 降至4.95L/100km与4.98L/100km。
- **电池：** 与现款相同，仍为18.3kWh与26.6kWh磷酸铁锂刀片电池。
- **尺寸与轴距：** 长宽高4775/1890/1670毫米，轴距2765毫米，均保持不变。

**原文未提及的项目：** DiLink 100、5G、轮毂、无线充电、方向盘加热等配置在这篇文章中都没有出现，无法确认。

**补充：** 文中提到的15万元起售价只是爆料的预扣提车价，并非正式官方价格。

**Date:** Launched August 19, 2024.

**New features vs. the predecessor:**
- **Wireless phone charging:** Added, with support for up to 50 W. The article says it "adds wireless charging for cell phones with up to 50 W power support."
- **Steering wheel heating:** Added. The article lists "support for steering wheel heating."
- **Cockpit:** Upgraded to the DiLink 100 system, described as "the latest DiLink 100 cockpit system with full support for 5G network connectivity across the range."
- **5G:** Now available on every variant. The predecessor offered 5G only on the top trim, with the others limited to 4G.

**Unchanged specs:**
- **Motors:** Entry variants have 150 kW and 310 Nm. The top variant has 160 kW and 330 Nm.
- **Range (CLTC):** 520 km on two variants and 605 km on the top variant.
- **Battery:** 71.8 kWh blade battery on the 520 km variants and 87.04 kWh on the top variant. The article gives no predecessor battery capacities, so it doesn't confirm any change.
- **Acceleration:** 0–50 km/h in 4.0 seconds, same as the predecessor.

**Pricing:** The entry price stays at RMB 149,800 ($20,980). The RMB 169,800 variant was dropped, and the top variant fell by RMB 14,000 (7.38%) from RMB 189,800 to RMB 175,800.

**Date:** January 1, 2025 (launch date; the article is dated Jan 1, 2025)

**Key differences from the Hi4-T (per the article):**

- **4WD structure:** The Hi4-Z uses a new "decoupled 4-wheel drive structure." GWM claims it offers superior off-road ability.
- **Battery placement and size:** On the Hi4-T, the battery sits under the trunk floor, which reduces trunk space and limits battery size. On the Hi4-Z, it sits in the chassis between the axles, allowing a 59.05 kWh pack.
- **EV range:** 201 km under WLTC.
- **DC fast charging:** 163 kW, which the article says is 60% higher than other PHEV off-road vehicles. A 30% to 80% charge takes about 15 minutes.
- **Discharge power:** Up to 600 kW.
- **Motors:** The front motor is rated at 215 kW and 400 Nm, and the rear at up to 240 kW and 415 Nm. The combined system output is 635 kW and 1,195 Nm peak torque.
- **Off-road specs:** 210 mm minimum ground clearance, 29° approach angle, and 24° departure angle.

**Carried over or largely unchanged:**

- **Engine and transmission:** The 2.0T E20NB Miller-cycle engine (185 kW, 380 Nm) with a three-speed hybrid DHT. The engine debuted in 2024.
- **Performance:** 0-100 km/h in 4.6 seconds. Fuel consumption is 8.6 L/100km.
- **Comprehensive range:** 1,096 km under WLTC.
- **Interior:** Largely the same as the Hi4-T, including a 12.3-inch instrument display, 14.6-inch infotainment screen, streaming rear-view mirror, head-up display, and Coffee OS 3.0.
- **Exterior:** Identical to the Hi4-T apart from badging. Dimensions are 5,078 × 1,934 × 1,905 mm with a 2,850 mm wheelbase.

**Other notes:**

- **Price:** 363,800 yuan (about 49,850 USD), one configuration only.
- **Rear suspension:** Retains the multi-link integral axle.
- **Colors:** Four options, including a white-to-red gradient.

The article does not give Hi4-T figures for power, torque, or range, so numeric comparisons beyond battery and motor specs aren't possible from this source.

- **EREV performance:** Single-motor, rear-wheel drive; 0–100 km/h in 6.9 seconds; 200 km/h top speed.

- **Driver assistance (top variant):** LiDAR and DiPilot 300, same as the hybrid.

**Not covered in the article:** DiSus-C and any front fascia changes are not mentioned.

- 百公里加速7.6秒，综合油耗6.35L/100km。

- 缤越L后来新增了Battle版，指导价9.78万元，先享价8.78万元。外观加入碳纤维风格运动套件和大尾翼，内饰有麂皮包裹的座舱和竞速氛围灯。

The search confirms the core details of the 2025 AITO M9 update, with one caveat on the satellite system's name.

- **Launch date and four LiDARs:** Sales in China began March 20, 2025, when the updated M9 arrived with four LiDAR units instead of the single sensor on the earlier model. The updated Aito M9 full-size SUV from Seres and Huawei was launched in China with four LiDARs and a starting price of 469,800 yuan (64,970 USD). Earlier reporting had predicted three solid-state LiDARs, so the four-unit configuration was a change from that forecast. According to reports, the 2025 Aito M9 is expected to feature significant upgrades in its intelligent driving hardware system, adding three high-precision solid-state LiDARs and distributed 4D millimeter-wave radar.
- **Why the extra sensors matter:** Huawei's driving system uses the extra units to handle tighter situations. Thanks to four LiDAR sensors, it supports passing through park gates, roundabouts, and complex roads. Some of the added units are short-range sensors for the sides and rear. The 2025 AITO M9 now comes with four LiDAR units, including new short-range units for side and rear detection, enhancing situational awareness.
- **118 kW range extender:** The EREV version uses a refreshed 1.5-litre engine rated at 118 kW. The extended-range version adopts a new range extender with an engine code of HG15T and a power output of 118kW. The BEV variant is separate. The pure electric version employs a dual-motor layout, with the front motor delivering a maximum power of 160kW and the rear motor providing up to 230kW.
- **Satellite communication:** The M9 has Huawei's satellite connectivity, which keeps the car online when terrestrial networks drop out. Sources differ on the name. Wikipedia calls it Xinghe, and says it can be shared with devices within a 30-metre (100 ft) range of the vehicle. A launch report describes it as the Huawei Galaxy satellite communication model, which allows continuous driving calls. The name is likely the same system described under different branding, but I couldn't confirm that from these results.
- **Battery change:** The EREV's smaller pack was dropped. Now, this vehicle is available with a 52 kWh ternary NMC pack, suitable for 290 km of electric range under CLTC conditions.

**Changes in the 2025 Aito M9 vs. the previous model**

- **LiDARs:** "four LiDARs instead of one sensor of the previous model." The 192-line spec is not stated.
- **ADS version:** Not stated. The article says only "new driving assistance system," which "supports passing through park gates, roundabouts, and complex roads."
- **Satellite comms:** "Huawei Galaxy satellite communication model, which allows continuous driving calls."
- **Projector resolution:** Not stated. The article mentions only "an upgraded projector."
- **Dimmable windows:** Not mentioned.
- **Range extender:** The 1.5-liter turbocharged petrol unit's "power output was boosted to 118 kW (158 hp)." The "HG15T" name does not appear.
- **Battery and range:** "The previously available 42 kWh battery was discontinued." The new "52 kWh ternary NMC pack" is "suitable for 290 km of electric range under CLTC conditions."
- **Seats:** The model is "available with five- and six-seat layout variants," and the article says the interior "aligns with its predecessor," so the seating is not described as new.
- **Other:**
  - "power thigh support for the driver’s seat"
  - "a new storage box with cooling and heating functions"
  - "new optional 21-inch rims"
  - "a new red body shade with beige-colored A and D pillars"
  - A "cross-level parking valet function" with ramp, uphill, downhill, and curve recognition

**2025 Denza D9 vs. 2024 D9: new features**

- **LiDAR:** "the addition of a roof lidar" supports the "God's Eye" system.
- **God's Eye BAS 3.0+:** "The entire series is equipped with BYD's 'God's Eye' BAS 3.0+ advanced driving assistance system."
- **DiPilot 300:** Not mentioned in the article.
- **Sensors:** "There are a total of 32 sensors throughout the car."
- **Chip:** Not mentioned in the article.
- **Front passenger screen:** The article lists "a co-pilot entertainment screen has been" but the sentence is cut off, so the change isn't specified.
- **Zero-gravity 2nd-row seats:** "the second-row seats have been upgraded to zero-gravity seats"
- **Power 3rd-row seats:** "the third-row seats support electric adjustment"
- **DM 5.0:** The PHEV uses "BYD's fifth-generation DM technology." Engine power rises "an increase of 13 kW (17 hp)" to 115 kW (154 hp). The front motor gains "30 kW (40 hp)" versus 2024.
- **Battery:**
  - PHEV: "39.938 kWh BYD Blade LFP battery pack," with a CLTC electric range of 200 km (FWD) and 190 km (AWD).
  - EV: "103 kWh BYD Blade LFP battery pack," with ranges of 620 km and 600 km.
  - EV charging: "800V platform as standard," with "shorten the 0% to 80% fast charging time to 7 minutes."
  - The article gives no 2024 battery figures for comparison.
- **Design:** The "appearance remains largely the same." Changes include "new 18-inch multi-spoke aluminum alloy rims" and "a new paint called Starry Gray." The "wheelbase is 3110 mm, which is 20 mm shorter" than the 2024 model.

BYD released the second-generation Yuan PLUS Intelligent Driving Edition on March 5, 2025, with five variants priced from 115,800 to 145,800 yuan. The updated Yuan PLUS keeps a design similar to the previous version, with changes limited to chrome trim on the side skirts and C-pillar, redesigned wheels, and a refreshed rear bumper.

Links: [{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/news/202411/1301610.html"},{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/news/202408/1300011.html"},{"title":"瑞虎7 PLUS-全部分类","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/6288/0/0-0-4-1/"},{"title":"换新前脸,搭1.6T动力,升级8AT, 2025款奇瑞瑞虎7 PLUS发布","url":"https://db.m.auto.sohu.com/model_6549/microEval"},{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/news/202410/1301525.html"},{"title":"IT之家 11 月 1 日消息,奇瑞官方今晚宣布,全新瑞虎 7 PLUS、瑞虎 7 高能版、瑞虎 7 C-DM 上市,指导价 9.99 万元起:","url":"https://www.ithome.com/0/807/319.htm"},{"title":"IT之家 10 月 26 日消息,奇瑞宣布旗下 2025 款瑞虎 7 PLUS 和瑞虎 7 高能版(含瑞虎 7 C-DM)将于 11 月 1 日正式上市。","url":"https://www.ithome.com/0/805/440.htm"},{"title":"瑞虎7 PLUS-车闻","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/6288/1/0-0-2-0/"},{"title":"www.zhichepai.com","url":"https://www.zhichepai.com/news/11029.html"}]

2024年11月的这次改款是2025款瑞虎7 PLUS，核心变化是外观焕新和动力升级为8AT。

**上市时间与价格**
- 奇瑞于11月1日上市新款瑞虎7 PLUS和瑞虎7高能版，瑞虎7 PLUS共推出4款车型，售价9.99-12.99万元。
- 1.6T 8AT的车型是尊贵型，指导价12.99万元，是该系列售价最高的版本。四款车型分别为1.6TGDI+7DCT 舒适型9.99万元、豪华型10.99万元、尊贵型11.99万元，以及1.6TGDI+8AT 尊贵型12.99万元。

**动力与8AT新增**
- 全系标配1.6TGDI鲲鹏动力发动机，最大功率145kW，峰值扭矩290N·m，搭配8AT变速器，最高机械效率达96%。奇瑞称这是首次把8AT变速箱带到10万级SUV。
- 资料对8AT的来源说法不一：搜狐报道称是奇瑞自研的"浮祯8AT"，而IT之家称为"鲲鹏8AT"，两者的具体名称需以官方信息为准。

**外观变化**
- 前脸：采用全新钻石星辉前格栅设计，大尺寸中网配点阵式设计，前大灯与中网相连。
- 尾部：采用全新的贯穿式尾灯，后包围取消了双边排气装饰，两侧新增运动感的装饰件。
- 侧面：第三排车窗样式经过优化。
- 内饰：延续现款车型的设计，采用双联屏的设计，中央配备水晶挡把，内饰变化不大。

**车身尺寸**
- 长宽高分别为4530x1862x1695mm，轴距2670mm。

**后续说明**
- 搜索结果显示，之后还有2026款瑞虎7高能版和瑞虎7 PLUS于2025年6月上市，并新增1.5T动力，因此2024年11月的这版已属于前一代改款。

如需确认最新配置表或购车政策，建议查看奇瑞官网或当地经销商信息。

Links: [{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/news/202504/1305114.html"},{"title":"www.ithome.com","url":"https://www.ithome.com/0/846/390.htm"},{"title":"IT之家 3 月 25 日消息,2025 款捷途旅行者 SUV 今日发布,官方指导价 13.99 万元起。","url":"https://www.ithome.com/0/840/596.htm"},{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/ask/25705604.html"},{"title":"chejiahao.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://chejiahao.autohome.com.cn/info/19669641"},{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/6606/0/0-0-3-0/"},{"title":"model 6865","url":"https://db.auto.sohu.com/model_6865"},{"title":"www.ithome.com","url":"https://www.ithome.com/0/839/927.htm"},{"title":"www.autohome.com.cn","url":"https://www.autohome.com.cn/ask/25632197.html"}]

2025款捷途旅行者于2025年3月25日上市,官方指导价13.99万元起。其中的"7+X"指的是越野模式,不是座位数。

**上市概况**
- 据IT之家报道,捷途汽车宣布2025款捷途旅行者将于3月25日上市,该车外观有所改进,仍可选1.5/2.0T发动机。
- 汽车之家称,2025款捷途旅行者正式上市,共推出7款车型,售价13.99-18.49万元。IT之家列出的价格则为13.99万至18.49万元之间的各版本(含2.0TD XWD征服 +的18.49万元版本)。

**7+X一键越野模式**
- 这是本款的主要升级点之一。IT之家指出,相较现款的6+X模式,新车将泥沙模式进行了细分,可选泥地模式和沙地模式。
- 因此"7+X"是一键越野模式的名称,数字7和6代表模式的档位数,与座位无关。

**50W无线充电与全速域自适应巡航**
- 这两项配置出现在2025款悦野版的介绍中。汽车之家报道,该版本售价19.19万元,定位紧凑型SUV,作为高配车型,相较在售车型新增尾门折叠桌。
- 同一篇报道中列出的配置包括50W手机无线充电、全速自适应巡航等。
- 搜索结果未明确说明这两项配置是否在2025款所有版本中标配,具体需以官方配置表为准。

**其他参考**
- 加长版(2025年4月18日上市)采用2.0T动力 + 七座布局,官方指导价17.99万元起,同样配有7+X一键越野模式。
- 动力方面,悦野版配备2.0T+7挡双离合动力组合,最大功率254马力,拥有XWD全自动智能四驱系统。

如需某一具体版本的完整配置,建议查看捷途官网或汽车之家的参数页面。

2025款比亚迪汉于2024年9月9日上市,主要升级包括激光雷达智驾版、800V纯电平台和云辇-C。

- **上市时间与价格:** 2025款汉EV和DM-i同日上市,2025款汉EV共推出4款车型,售价为17.98万~23.58万元;2025款汉DM-i共推出5款车型,售价为16.58万~22.58万元。
- **激光雷达:** 汽车之家称该款是王朝网首个搭载激光雷达的高阶智能驾驶辅助车型,搭载的是DiPilot 300"天神之眼"系统。其中,高配车型搭载DiPilot 300(天神之眼B),硬件包含1颗126线激光雷达、5颗毫米波雷达、7颗智驾摄像头和英伟达Orin-X芯片。该数据来自一篇发布于2026年的购车文章,属二手汇总信息。
- **800V:** 新款汉的电动版采用800V架构。顶配701km/705km版本升级全域800V高压平台,30%-80%快充仅需20分钟,其中快充时间同样来自该购车文章,需要注意其可靠性。
- **云辇-C:** 新车搭载比亚迪第五代DM技术、DiPilot 300、云辇-C(高配车型)并换装了后五连杆悬架等。云辇-C是智能阻尼车身控制系统,中高配升级云辇-C智能阻尼控制系统,过颠簸路面时车身更稳、后排更舒适。
- **底盘:** 2025款汉取消了原有"筷子悬架",改为后五连杆独立悬架(见 ifanr 与汽车之家报道)。
- **后续更新:** 2025款汉与汉智驾版激光雷达系列开启新一轮OTA升级,本次升级新增16项功能,并针对14项体验进行优化,该消息发布于2026年1月。

**来源冲突:** 一篇发布于2026年7月的购车文章称该款车于2025年第二季度正式上市,与2024年9月的上市报道不符。多篇上市当日的报道一致指向2024年9月,因此应以2024年9月为准,该文的时间应为笔误或误写。
